You are a sidekick worker for the pi-gui repo (a Codex-style Electron desktop app for `pi`). You work in the git worktree you were started in (branch `lane/muse-cli-driver`, based on main 03c56e8b). Read AGENTS.md, docs/architecture.md, packages/pi-sdk-driver/AGENTS.md, and the section "Priority 1: Muse Code CLI as the sidekick runtime" in docs/lead-sidekick-optimization-plan.md. That section is your spec.

Implement plan items 9a and 9b in this order, as small focused commits (`git commit -m ... -- <paths>`):

1. New workspace package `packages/muse-cli-driver` (`@pi-gui/muse-cli-driver`). Model its package.json, tsconfig and build on packages/pi-sdk-driver, and add it to the pnpm workspace and to the root `build:shared` script.
   - It implements the `SessionDriver` interface from packages/session-driver/src/types.ts by spawning the official `muse` binary (`muse exec --json`), one process per turn, in its own process group, with a fixed `--session-id <uuid>` per session.
   - Map the MSP JSONL records (schema_version 1) to SessionDriver events and snapshots: run_started, run_output_delta (assistant text), task_lifecycle (tool rows where they represent tool calls; inspect fixtures), run_usage (usage), run_terminal (completed/failed/cancelled, final text).
   - Real recorded fixtures: /tmp/turn1.jsonl (first turn) and /tmp/turn2-followup.jsonl (follow-up in the same session). Copy them into the package's test/fixtures.
   - Implement the unsupported operations (fork, tree navigation, compaction, etc.) by rejecting with a clear error.
   - Implement cancel and rescue as SIGTERM to the process group, then SIGKILL after a few seconds.
   - `openSession` after a restart rebuilds the transcript via `muse export --session <id> --out <tmpfile>`. Check the export JSON shape with the echo provider.
   - The binary path is configurable and defaults to `muse` on PATH, then ~/.local/bin/muse.
   - Pass options through to flags: model, reasoning effort, cwd/workspace, worktree existing path, scout => `--disable-write`, `--approval-mode never`, `--trust-workspace`.
   - Tests use node:test. The mapping tests run over the fixtures. Add one integration test against the real binary with `--provider echo`, which is deterministic and offline. Skip it if `muse` isn't installed.
2. Desktop routing (9b). The desktop app currently uses a single pi-sdk-driver SessionDriver. Add a small router that sends sessions tagged with runtime "muse-cli" to the Muse driver and everything else to pi-sdk-driver. In apps/desktop/electron/orchestration/app-store-orchestration.ts `createChildThreadRecord`, tag a child as muse-cli when its sidekick or scout model provider is `meta` and the Meta credential is an OAuth subscription; ~/.pi/agent/auth.json has meta.type == "oauth", so read it through existing pi auth helpers if available. Add an env override `PI_APP_SIDEKICK_RUNTIME=pi|muse-cli|auto` (default auto). Persist the runtime tag on the child record so restarts route correctly; follow the UI-state migration rules in docs/architecture.md. The child must stay an ordinary thread: sidebar, rail, child report, rescue, worktree, reuse and budget all work.

Constraints: keep the renderer/main/preload boundary tight. Never talk to Meta's API directly and never reproduce Muse Code's tool declarations; only shell out to the official binary. No full test suites. Wrap long commands so they can't hang forever.

Verify: build the new package plus its node tests; `pnpm --dir apps/desktop run typecheck`; `node --test scripts/state-owner-boundary.test.mjs`; the relevant desktop unit specs via `pnpm exec playwright test -c apps/desktop/playwright.config.ts <files>`.

Finish with a report under 1200 characters: commits, what was verified, what is left (settings UI 9c and serve 9d are out of scope), and risks.

Read text file `AGENTS.md`.
1|# Repo Guidelines
2|
3|These rules apply for the full session.
4|
5|## Workflow
6|
7|- Define success criteria before coding; if unclear, stop and clarify.
8|- For non-trivial work, plan verification before editing: name the affected user flow, observable result, failure cases, and smallest existing command that proves them. Start with the checked-in [desktop verification skill](.agents/skills/verify-pi-gui/SKILL.md) for desktop flows and [baseline checks](docs/ci-baseline.md) for repository checks. Do not run tests to discover what to run.
9|- Run fewer and only necessary tests by default: no test commands until the plan is stated; prefer one scoped lane/spec/filter over full suites. Full suites (for example `pnpm check`, `pnpm test:baseline`, `pnpm test:guards`, `test:e2e:all`, unfiltered `swift test`, `xcodebuild test`, or any whole-repo run) are opt-in only with justification, pre-merge, or explicit user request. CI already covers the full baseline.
10|- Do not create or switch to new branches to start work unless the user explicitly asks; respect the current branch or worktree as intentional.
11|- Commit in small focused checkpoints; don’t batch unrelated changes.
12|- Before closing non-trivial implementation work, review the diff for unnecessary abstractions, duplicate paths, unsafe escapes, and obsolete code; simplify within scope and run only the checks named in the plan.
13|
14|## Product
15|
16|- This repo is building a Codex-style desktop app for `pi`; preserve that product direction.
17|- Desktop work is not done until it is verified on the real Electron surface, not only by unit tests.
18|- Transcript/timeline behavior, session correctness, and Codex-style UX are product features, not polish.
19|- Prefer clean reimplementation over patching around local complexity.
20|
21|## Safety
22|
23|- Never delete user session history, cached transcripts, screenshots, or temp artifacts without approval.
24|- Treat files you didn’t edit as read-only when multiple agents may be working.
25|- Ask before destructive commands or history rewrites.
26|
27|## Structure
28|
29|- Prefer path-scoped guidance in nested `AGENTS.md` files over growing this file.
30|- Follow the ownership and migration guidance in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md); target folders are not evidence that a migration is complete.
31|- Keep the desktop renderer/main/preload boundary tight; avoid broad Node exposure to the renderer.
32|- Keep `pi-sdk-driver` thin over `pi-mono`; don’t fork or reimplement `pi` runtime behavior unless necessary.
33|
34|## Source Of Truth
35|
36|- Root `AGENTS.md` is the repo instruction source of truth.
37|- Root `CLAUDE.md` should remain a symlink to `AGENTS.md`.

payload.text:
Done. Two commits on `lane/muse-cli-driver`:

- `[b4f2dd0](https://github.com/minghinmatthewlam/pi-gui/commit/b4f2dd025f2d27b0003d1d9882e64854ecc7c534)` 9a: `packages/muse-cli-driver` (`@pi-gui/muse-cli-driver`) — `SessionDriver` over `muse exec --json`, one process per turn in its own group, fixed `--session-id`; MSP→event mapping; fixtures copied to `test/fixtures`; SIGTERM→SIGKILL cancel/rescue; `openSession` via `muse export`; in `build:shared`, lint and host-boundary gates.
- `[9f377fe](https://github.com/minghinmatthewlam/pi-gui/commit/9f377feeb5a98688fe133868b6b2d0e23345666b)` 9b: `SessionDriverRouter` (muse-cli vs pi by child tag), `runtime` on the child record (UI-state v22, absent means pi), `PI_APP_SIDEKICK_RUNTIME` override, auto via meta model + OAuth (runtime snapshot, else `auth.json`) + binary check.

Verified: 15/15 package tests (fixture mapping, echo integration incl. export rebuild, stub kill paths); desktop typecheck; state-owner/host-boundary/contract guards; 12/12 new unit spec; ~255 related orchestration/persistence specs green. Key find: export uses a different record vocabulary than the live stream — the parser handles both; cancel settles quietly like pi.

Left: settings UI (9c), `muse serve` (9d), one real subscription run, Electron-surface check. Risks: tool-task shape for real tool calls is inferred (`tool.*` discriminator) — fixtures contain none; 2 pre-existing eslint errors in orchestration file left untouched; forced `muse-cli` with no binary fails at first turn with a clear install error.
